comparator.academicYear: 2026-2027 current programme and course records; 2023 curriculum phased in through year 3 in 2025-2026; checked 2026-10-05
comparator.sourceNotes: The current TU/e programme and degree-structure pages establish the 180-EC bachelor, its behavioural-science and behavioural-research core, three technical specialisations, challenge-based work, elective space and Bachelor Final Project. The September 2025 NVAO accreditation report reproduces the current curriculum table introduced for starters from 2023-2024 and phased through the third year in 2025-2026. That table accounts for 180 EC as 36 five-credit quarter slots, with the Bachelor Final Project occupying two slots. It identifies the named Psychology & Technology, research-methods, data, ITEC and challenge courses, six technical-specialisation slots (30 EC), 45 EC of electives and a 10-EC final project. Robotics is instantiated by the neutral official-order rule; the route component is preserved as one 30-EC restricted specialisation block because the public curriculum table labels its six positions as Technical Course rather than supplying a current route-specific list.

alternatives.label: Psychology, cognition & human-technology interaction
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum visibly combines psychology, cognition and behavioural research with programming, data, AI, computer vision and robotics.
alternatives.concept: The closest UCR response combines psychology and cognitive science with behavioural research, programming, data analysis, machine learning, computer vision, robotics and responsible AI. It reproduces the human-technology and research core as closely as UCR permits while keeping TU/e's dedicated engineering specialisation, challenge projects and Bachelor Final Project visible as limits.
progression: Psychology, programming, data and research foundations precede machine learning, advanced behavioural methods, computer vision, higher cognition, robotics, deep learning and advanced AI. Formal prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort offerings pass; ten 300-level courses are included.

alternatives.label: Behaviour, responsible technology & digital society
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum keeps psychology and research methods while shifting substantial space toward product design, technology adoption, organisations, communication, responsible AI and digital society.
alternatives.concept: This distinct route studies how people adopt, resist and are affected by digital and automated systems. It combines psychology, cognition and empirical user research with product design, communication, sociology, organisations, digital transformation and AI ethics, producing a social and responsible-innovation route rather than a second technical AI curriculum.
progression: Programming, data, psychology, research and design foundations precede machine learning, higher cognition, persuasive communication, organisational psychology, applied user research, business uses of AI and contemporary social theory. Formal prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort offerings pass; eight 300-level courses are included.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the closest route, this curriculum replaces more than four neuroscience, advanced AI, computer-vision, robotics and mathematical courses with product design, user and market research, sociology, communication, organisational psychology, digital transformation and societal analysis. Each route has thirteen courses not present in the other.

blocks: Introduction to Brain & Behavior supplies broad psychological and neuroscientific foundations, but not the target course's dedicated technology framing.
Social Psychology directly addresses social influence and behaviour; TU/e also gives environmental psychology dedicated coverage.
Neurobiology provides a biological account of brain and behaviour.
Higher Order Functions studies attention, memory, executive functions and decision processes.
Perception & Action closely addresses perception, action and sensorimotor interaction.
Medical & Health Psychology addresses behaviour and wellbeing, but not the full digital-tools component.
Introduction to Programming provides the computational foundation used in behavioural technology work.
Introduction to Data Science develops applied data preparation and visualisation.
Research Methods & Statistics covers research design, experiments, surveys and inference.
Statistics & Experimental Methods provides psychology-specific experimental and multivariate methods.
Market Research includes applied user research, but is not an equivalent qualitative psychology project.
Advanced Research Seminar develops evidence synthesis and independent research design.
Probability & Statistics supports quantitative behavioural analysis but is not a dedicated research project.
Mathematical Methods covers calculus and quantitative modelling.
Robotics addresses sensing, movement and autonomous systems, but one UCR course cannot reproduce the 30-EC TU/e robotics specialisation.
Decision-making in AI examines intelligent-agent behaviour; TU/e adds explicit human-centred design and evaluation.
AI Ethics directly addresses responsible design, fairness, privacy and accountability.
Consumer Product Design provides one team-based design and prototyping experience, but not TU/e's multidisciplinary engineering challenge.
Introduction to Sociology addresses institutions and social relations; TU/e adds dedicated social-network analysis.
UCR distributes societal and ethical analysis across several courses; no single scheduled course reproduces this ITEC component.
Elective space, formation and final project
TU/e preserves 45 EC of genuine elective space; the displayed UCR pathways are complete fixed examples.
TU/e requires a 10-EC Bachelor Final Project. UCR optional independent research is shown separately.

candidates.label: Responsible technology, social behaviour and adoption
Environmental psychology and built environments
candidates.reason: UCR offers perception, social psychology, sustainability and urban-society courses, but no environmental-psychology sequence, building science, architectural design studio, lighting and acoustics, spatial modelling or built-environment technology progression from which to construct a separate 24-course programme without replacing the target strand with general sustainability and social-science study.

selection.assessment: The closest programme is a defensible psychology-and-human-technology response with behavioural methods, data, AI and robotics. A second coherent curriculum follows the explicit responsible-design, technology-adoption and social-consequences cluster and passes all qualitative and pairwise distinctness rules. The remaining Living and built-environment direction was tested but UCR lacks the environmental-psychology and built-environment sequence needed to sustain it as a third 24-course programme.

routeSelection.basis: The generic target does not select between the current Robotics, ICT and Living technical specialisations. Current programme descriptions list Robotics first and do not establish one route as broader or more representative, so the neutral official-order tie-break selects Robotics without reference to UCR fit.

notes.text: TU/e integrates behavioural science and research with a 30-EC technical specialisation, named research projects, multidisciplinary challenge-based engineering, Impact of Technology courses, 45 EC of genuine electives and a required Bachelor Final Project. UCR offers strong psychology, cognitive science, research methods, data, AI, computer vision, robotics, design, communication and social analysis, but neither route reproduces TU/e's six-course engineering specialisation, sensors-and-control formation, repeated challenge projects, dedicated environmental-psychology and built-environment sequence or compulsory final project.
